To calculate your taxable income, start by determining your gross income (total earnings) and subtract eligible deductions (such as mortgage payments, childcare expenses, or retirement contributions). This gives you your taxable income, which is then used to apply the appropriate tax rate. For example, if your gross income is $60,000 and your deductions total $10,000, your taxable income would be $50,000. The tax liability is then calculated by multiplying this figure by the federal tax rate (e.g., 24% for the 2023 tax year). This step ensures you account for all allowable deductions before determining your final tax obligation.

The filing process requires accuracy in reporting your income and expenses to avoid penalties. For instance, if your taxable income is $50,000 and your tax rate is 24%, your tax liability would be $12,000. Proper filing ensures your return is processed efficiently and your tax payments are accurate.
